top_categories.workout_context: When someone attacks on steep paved highway climb, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Mount Baker Hill Climb's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.

Road-specific control matters at Mount Baker Hill Climb. Practice on steep paved highway climb: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 22 miles.
At Mount Baker Hill Climb, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Varied gradients on steep paved highway climb demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
203ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
22 miles on steep paved highway climb burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Mount Baker Hill Climb. Train it until it feels boring.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Mount Baker Hill Climb. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 4,462ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on steep paved highway climb can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Base fitness for Mount Baker Hill Climb. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.

race_overlay.weather: September in Glacier, Washington, USA — September delivers relatively dry conditions perfect for grinding uphill amid stunning vistas. Cooler temps at elevation keep you from melting, but variability demands layers. Views of snow-capped peaks rarely disappoint unless fog rolls in. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before Mount Baker Hill Climb. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan that matches the ride duration, intensity, weather, and confirmed resupply points.
race_overlay.altitude: Mount Baker Hill Climb reaches approximately 5,100ft above sea level. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. High-altitude chill post-climb.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Mount Baker Hill Climb rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on steep paved highway climb to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Race Simulation, and Road Specific to prepare you for 22 miles of steep paved highway climb in Glacier, Washington, USA.
